usb-ports.gadgetZero.note: A device's name (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab, messages about attaching): the controller's built-in test device, attached with ?usbzero=1.

usb-ports.builtinKeyboard.note: A device's name (USB menu, messages about attaching): the machine's own USB boot keyboard on the last connector, which carries the screen's keys to the firmware.

usb-ports.testDevice.note: A device's name for a virtual test device of another kind, where a sentence names the device ("… couldn't be attached"); lowercase, as it may stand mid-sentence.

usb-ports.gamepad.note: A device's name (USB menu, messages about attaching, Snapshot's question): the emulated USB game pad fed by one of your computer's game pads through the Gamepad API; {{name}} is that game pad's name as the browser gives it.

usb-ports.gamepad.unnamed.note: {{name}} of usb-ports.gamepad when the browser gives the host's game pad no name.

usb-ports.usbDevice.note: A WebUSB device's name when it gives no product name (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab, messages). {{ids}} is its vendor and product IDs as lsusb prints them, e.g. 2e8a:000a.

usb-ports.hidDevice.note: A WebHID device's name when it gives no product name (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab, messages). {{ids}} is its vendor and product IDs as lsusb prints them, e.g. 054c:0ce6.

usb-problems.class.audio.note: A USB interface class's name (audio), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.cdc.note: A USB interface class's name (communications (CDC)), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.hid.note: A USB interface class's name (HID), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.stillImage.note: A USB interface class's name (still image), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.printer.note: A USB interface class's name (printer), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.massStorage.note: A USB interface class's name (mass storage), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.hub.note: A USB interface class's name (hub), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.cdcData.note: A USB interface class's name (CDC data), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.smartCard.note: A USB interface class's name (smart card), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.video.note: A USB interface class's name (video), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.audioVideo.note: A USB interface class's name (audio/video), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.bluetooth.note: A USB interface class's name (wireless controller (Bluetooth)), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.dfu.note: A USB interface class's name (DFU), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.vendor.note: A USB interface class's name (vendor-specific), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.class.other.note: A USB interface class without a name of its own, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't see interface N, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps." (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab). {{code}} is the class number in hex, e.g. 0x05.

usb-problems.usage.pointer.note: A HID collection's kind (pointer), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't get the device's {{what}} part…" about a HID device (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.usage.mouse.note: A HID collection's kind (mouse), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't get the device's {{what}} part…" about a HID device (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.usage.keyboard.note: A HID collection's kind (keyboard), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't get the device's {{what}} part…" about a HID device (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.usage.keypad.note: A HID collection's kind (keypad), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't get the device's {{what}} part…" about a HID device (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.usage.systemControl.note: A HID collection's kind (system control), lowercase, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't get the device's {{what}} part…" about a HID device (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab).

usb-problems.usage.other.note: A HID collection without a name of its own, placed in the problem "The guest doesn't get the device's {{what}} part…". {{usage}} is its usage page and usage in hex, e.g. 000c:0001.

usb-problems.protectedInterface.hid.message: The guest doesn't see interface {{interface}}, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps. To pass its HID part through, use Add a device… › A HID device (WebHID) instead. A keyboard's keys and a mouse's pointer can't be passed through either way; your keyboard and mouse reach the machine through this emulator anyway.
usb-problems.protectedInterface.hid.note: A problem under a WebUSB device attached with part of it left out (Machines page's USB tab, the USB menu's tooltip, an attach's error). {{interface}} is the interface number; {{class}} its class's name (usb-problems.class.*), read as a plural ("audio interfaces"). This variant is for a HID interface: it says where to go instead (the menu path is the Add a USB device wizard's words).

usb-problems.protectedInterface.disk.message: The guest doesn't see interface {{interface}}, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps. Add a disk image to the machine's Disks instead.
usb-problems.protectedInterface.disk.note: A problem under a WebUSB device attached with part of it left out (Machines page's USB tab, the USB menu's tooltip, an attach's error). {{interface}} is the interface number; {{class}} its class's name (usb-problems.class.*), read as a plural ("audio interfaces"). This variant is for a mass storage interface.

usb-problems.protectedInterface.sound.message: The guest doesn't see interface {{interface}}, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps. Sound goes through the machine's own sound card instead, which can also record from your computer's microphone.
usb-problems.protectedInterface.sound.note: A problem under a WebUSB device attached with part of it left out (Machines page's USB tab, the USB menu's tooltip, an attach's error). {{interface}} is the interface number; {{class}} its class's name (usb-problems.class.*), read as a plural ("audio interfaces"). This variant is for an audio or video interface.

usb-problems.protectedInterface.bluetoot.message: The guest doesn't see interface {{interface}}, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps. No browser lets a web app use a Bluetooth adapter.
usb-problems.protectedInterface.bluetoot.note: A problem under a WebUSB device attached with part of it left out (Machines page's USB tab, the USB menu's tooltip, an attach's error). {{interface}} is the interface number; {{class}} its class's name (usb-problems.class.*), read as a plural ("audio interfaces"). This variant is for a Bluetooth adapter.

usb-problems.protectedInterface.message: The guest doesn't see interface {{interface}}, because this browser keeps {{class}} interfaces from web apps.
usb-problems.protectedInterface.note: A problem under a WebUSB device attached with part of it left out (Machines page's USB tab, the USB menu's tooltip, an attach's error). {{interface}} is the interface number; {{class}} its class's name (usb-problems.class.*), read as a plural ("audio interfaces"). This variant is for any other class (no route elsewhere).

usb-problems.browserSaid.note: Line under a USB problem's folded details (Machines page's USB tab, Add a USB device, the USB menu's error): the browser's own error message. {{said}} is that message, in the browser's words.

usb-problems.zadig.message: Install the WinUSB driver for the device with Zadig. In Zadig, select Options › List All Devices, select the device, choose WinUSB, then select Replace Driver.
usb-problems.zadig.note: Step 1 of the Windows remedy under a USB problem (folded, with a link to zadig.akeo.ie): how to give the device the driver a browser needs. Zadig's menu items are named as Zadig names them.

usb-problems.zadig.interface.message: Install the WinUSB driver for the interface with Zadig. In Zadig, select Options › List All Devices, select the device's interface {{interface}}, choose WinUSB, then select Replace Driver.
usb-problems.zadig.interface.note: Step 1 of the Windows remedy for an interface something else holds (folded under the problem, with a link to zadig.akeo.ie). {{interface}} is the interface number.

usb-problems.replug.message: Unplug the device, plug it in again, then attach it.
usb-problems.replug.note: Last step of a USB remedy (Windows' driver, Linux's udev rule), numbered in the folded details under the problem.

usb-problems.claimFailed.message: Interface {{interface}} doesn't reach the guest, because something on your computer is already using it.
usb-problems.claimFailed.note: A USB problem's short text (Machines page's USB tab, USB menu, an attach's error): a driver or program on the user's computer holds an interface; the OS's remedy is folded under it. {{interface}} is the interface number.

usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.message: How to free it on Linux
usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.note: Title of the folded remedy (a summary to click) under the problem "Interface N doesn't reach the guest, because something on your computer is already using it.", when the user's computer runs Linux.

usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.driver.message: Find the kernel driver that holds the interface, such as cdc_acm, ftdi_sio, cp210x, ch341, or usblp:
usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.driver.note: Step 1 of the Linux remedy for an interface a driver holds; a command to copy (lsusb -t) follows. The driver names are Linux's.

usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.name.message: Find the interface's name under that driver, such as {{name}}:
usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.name.note: Step 2 of the Linux remedy for an interface a driver holds; a command to copy follows. {{name}} is an example of a sysfs interface name, e.g. 1-2:1.0.

usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.unbind.message: Unbind the driver from it. The interface stays free until the device is plugged in again:
usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.unbind.note: Step 3 of the Linux remedy for an interface a driver holds; the unbind command to copy follows.

usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.again.note: Step 4, the last, of the Linux remedy for an interface a driver holds.

usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.blacklist.message: To keep the driver off for good, for every device it serves, add this line to a file in /etc/modprobe.d/:
usb-problems.claimFailed.linux.blacklist.note: Note after the Linux remedy's steps for an interface a driver holds; the line to add (blacklist <driver>) follows.

usb-problems.claimFailed.mac.note: Title of the folded remedy under the problem "Interface N doesn't reach the guest, because something on your computer is already using it.", on a Mac.

usb-problems.claimFailed.mac.quit.message: Quit any app that uses the device, then attach it again.
usb-problems.claimFailed.mac.quit.note: The one step of the macOS remedy for an interface something holds.

usb-problems.claimFailed.mac.note.message: macOS's own drivers may hold serial devices, such as CDC serial devices, and a web app can't take a device from them. If one of those drivers holds it, the device can't reach the machine from your computer.
usb-problems.claimFailed.mac.note.note: Note after the macOS remedy's step for an interface something holds.

usb-problems.claimFailed.windows.message: How to free it on Windows
usb-problems.claimFailed.windows.note: Title of the folded remedy under the problem "Interface N doesn't reach the guest, because something on your computer is already using it.", on Windows (Zadig's steps follow).

usb-problems.claimFailed.windows.note.message: After this, programs on your computer that used the old driver no longer see that interface.
usb-problems.claimFailed.windows.note.note: Note after the Windows remedy's steps (the WinUSB driver through Zadig) for an interface something holds.

usb-problems.claimFailed.other.message: Interface {{interface}} doesn't reach the guest, because something on your computer is already using it. Close what uses it, then attach the device again.
usb-problems.claimFailed.other.note: A USB problem's text on a computer without a remedy of its own (ChromeOS, other): a driver or program holds an interface. {{interface}} is the interface number.

usb-problems.protectedCollection.kept.message: The guest gets only the feature reports of the device's {{what}} part, the settings that tools such as VIA use. This browser keeps the rest of that part from web apps. Your keyboard and mouse reach the machine through this emulator anyway.
usb-problems.protectedCollection.kept.note: A problem under an attached WebHID device (Machines page's USB tab, USB menu's tooltip): one of its collections reaches the guest only through its feature reports. {{what}} is the collection's kind (usb-problems.usage.*).

usb-problems.protectedCollection.message: The guest doesn't get the device's {{what}} part, because this browser keeps it from web apps. Your keyboard and mouse reach the machine through this emulator anyway.
usb-problems.protectedCollection.note: A problem under an attached WebHID device (Machines page's USB tab, USB menu's tooltip): one of its collections doesn't reach the guest. {{what}} is the collection's kind (usb-problems.usage.*).

usb-problems.noCollections.message: None of this HID device reaches the guest. This browser keeps all of its parts from web apps, as it does with keyboards, mice, and security keys. Your keyboard and mouse reach the machine through this emulator anyway.
usb-problems.noCollections.note: A problem under a WebHID device that couldn't be attached (an attach's error in the USB menu, Add a USB device, the Machines page): nothing of it reaches pages.

usb-problems.openFailed.linux.message: This browser couldn't open the device. Your user account probably has no permission to use it.
usb-problems.openFailed.linux.note: A problem when a USB or HID device couldn't be opened, when the user's computer runs Linux (an attach's error); the udev remedy is folded under it, with the browser's own message.

usb-problems.openFailed.linux.title.message: How to give your user account access on Linux
usb-problems.openFailed.linux.title.note: Title of the folded remedy (a udev rule) under the problem "This browser couldn't open the device. Your user account probably has no permission to use it."

usb-problems.openFailed.linux.udev.note: Step 1 of the Linux remedy for a device the user may not open; the rule to copy follows.

usb-problems.openFailed.linux.reload.note: Step 2 of the Linux remedy for a device the user may not open; the command to copy follows.

usb-problems.openFailed.windows.message: This browser couldn't open the device. On Windows, it needs the WinUSB driver.
usb-problems.openFailed.windows.note: A problem when a WebUSB device couldn't be opened on Windows (an attach's error); Zadig's steps are folded under it.

usb-problems.openFailed.windows.title.note: Title of the folded remedy (installing WinUSB with Zadig) under the problem "This browser couldn't open the device. On Windows, it needs the WinUSB driver."

usb-problems.openFailed.other.message: This browser couldn't open the device. Another program may have it open; close that program, then attach the device again.
usb-problems.openFailed.other.note: A problem when a device couldn't be opened, on a computer without a remedy of its own (an attach's error); the browser's own message is folded under it.

usb-live.noWebUsb.message: This browser doesn't support WebUSB. Chromium and Google Chrome do.
usb-live.noWebUsb.note: Error (message bar, Add a USB device) when a USB device is to be picked in a browser without WebUSB.

usb-live.noWebHid.message: This browser doesn't support WebHID. Chromium and Google Chrome do.
usb-live.noWebHid.note: Error (message bar, Add a USB device) when a HID device is to be picked in a browser without WebHID.

usb-live.notAttached.note: Headline of an attach's error when the device worker said why (USB menu, Add a USB device, Machines page's USB tab, message bar): the problems and their remedies follow under it. {{name}} is the device's name.

usb-live.noAnswer.message: The machine's USB controller didn't answer. Check that the machine is still running.
usb-live.noAnswer.note: Error when an attach or a detach got no answer from the running machine in time (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab, message bar).

usb-live.connectorTaken.message: {{name}} is on connector {{connector}}. Detach it first.
usb-live.connectorTaken.note: Error when a device is attached on a connector another device is on (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab). {{connector}} is the connector's number (from 1); {{name}} the device on it.

usb-live.connectorInUse.note: Error when another device took the connector while this one waited for its lock (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab). {{connector}} is the connector's number (from 1).

usb-live.stopped.note: Error of an attach or a detach still waiting when the machine stopped (USB menu, Machines page's USB tab, message bar).

usb.noWebUsb.message: WebUSB isn't available to the machine.
usb.noWebUsb.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu): the machine's device worker has no WebUSB to open the device with. A full sentence: it is a line under a headline.

usb.noWebHid.message: WebHID isn't available to the machine.
usb.noWebHid.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu): the machine's device worker has no WebHID to open the device with. A full sentence: it is a line under a headline.

usb.openFailed.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when the device worker couldn't open the device; why follows on the next line. A full sentence: it is a line under a headline.

usb.wentAway.message: The machine stopped while the device was being opened.
usb.wentAway.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu): the machine stopped while the device was being opened. A full sentence: it is a line under a headline.

webusb.openFailed.message: This browser couldn't open the device.
webusb.openFailed.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when the browser refused to open a USB or HID device; the browser's own words follow on the next line. A full sentence: it is a line under a headline.

webusb.readFailed.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when a WebUSB device's descriptors couldn't be read or its configuration set up; the browser's own words follow on the next line. A full sentence: it is a line under a headline.

webusb.noInterface.message: None of the device's interfaces can be used through WebUSB.
webusb.noInterface.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when every interface of a WebUSB device is kept from pages or held; the problems follow. A full sentence: it is a line under a headline.

webusb.notFound.message: The device isn't plugged in, or this web app has no permission to use it.
webusb.notFound.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when the remembered device isn't among those the browser lists now. A full sentence: it is a line under a headline.

webhid.noCollections.message: WebHID shows none of this device's collections.
webhid.noCollections.note: Detail of an attach's error (message bar, USB menu) when the browser hides all of a HID device. A full sentence: it is a line under a headline.

Usb.state.attached.note: A remembered USB device's state, at the end of its line on the Machines page's USB tab (lowercase, after ' · '): attached to the machine on this page.

Usb.state.plugged.note: A remembered USB device's state, at the end of its line on the Machines page's USB tab (lowercase, after ' · '): plugged into your computer, with permission, and attached nowhere.

Usb.state.unplugged.note: A remembered USB device's state, at the end of its line on the Machines page's USB tab (lowercase, after ' · '): granted but not plugged in now.

Usb.state.held.note: A remembered USB device's state, at the end of its line on the Machines page's USB tab (lowercase, after ' · '): attached to a machine in another tab that didn't say its name.

Usb.state.ungranted.note: A remembered USB device's state, at the end of its line on the Machines page's USB tab (lowercase, after ' · '): remembered, but this browser hasn't granted it (the machine came from another browser).

Usb.state.heldBy.note: A remembered USB device's state on the Machines page's USB tab: attached to another machine, in another tab. {{holder}} is that machine's name.

Usb.forget.attached.message: Forget {{name}}? It will be detached first, and the guest will see it unplugged. If no other machine remembers it, this browser's permission to use it will be removed too.
Usb.forget.attached.note: Question (confirm dialog) on the Machines page's USB tab when Forget is clicked on a device attached to the running machine. {{name}} is the device's name.

Usb.forget.message: Forget {{name}}? If no other machine remembers it, this browser's permission to use it will be removed too.
Usb.forget.note: Question (confirm dialog) on the Machines page's USB tab when Forget is clicked on a device not attached here. {{name}} is the device's name.

Usb.forget.title.note: Title of the confirm dialog that asks before a remembered USB device is forgotten (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.forget.ok.note: OK button of the confirm dialog that asks before a remembered USB device is forgotten.

Usb.busy.forgetting.note: What the Machines page is doing (shown with … at its top) while a USB device is forgotten.

Usb.noController.message: This machine has no USB controller. Turn it on above to attach devices.
Usb.noController.note: Note at the top of the Machines page's USB tab for a machine whose USB controller is off (the switch is above it) and that has no snapshots.

Usb.noController.orphans.message: This machine has no USB controller. Turn it on above to attach devices; snapshots taken before the change will be orphaned.
Usb.noController.orphans.note: Note at the top of the Machines page's USB tab for a machine whose USB controller is off (the switch is above it) and that has snapshots.

Usb.meta.usb.note: The start of a remembered WebUSB device's details line (Machines page, USB tab, under its name). {{ids}} is its vendor and product IDs, e.g. 2e8a:000a.

Usb.meta.hid.note: The start of a remembered WebHID device's details line (Machines page, USB tab, under its name). {{ids}} is its vendor and product IDs, e.g. 054c:0ce6.

Usb.meta.serial.note: Part of a remembered USB device's details line (Machines page, USB tab), after ' · ': its serial number, {{serial}}.

Usb.meta.index.nd.note: Part of a remembered USB device's details line (Machines page, USB tab), after ' · ', for the second of identical devices without a serial number ({{n}} is 2): English's ordinal suffix is in the words, so the page picks nd, rd or th.

Usb.meta.index.rd.note: Part of a remembered USB device's details line (Machines page, USB tab), after ' · ', for the third of identical devices without a serial number ({{n}} is 3).

Usb.meta.index.th.note: Part of a remembered USB device's details line (Machines page, USB tab), after ' · ', for the fourth or later of identical devices without a serial number ({{n}} is its place, 4 and up).

Usb.connector.title.message: The root connector the device is plugged into. It sets the device's port path in the guest, so its names under /dev/serial/by-path stay the same.
Usb.connector.title.note: Tooltip of a remembered USB device's Connector field (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.connector.note: Label of a remembered USB device's connector choice (1–4), on its line on the Machines page's USB tab.

Usb.busy.saving.note: What the Machines page is doing (shown with … at its top) while a USB device's connector or At start is saved.

Usb.atStart.title.message: Attach the device when the machine starts, and when the device is plugged in while the machine runs.
Usb.atStart.title.note: Tooltip of a remembered USB device's At start checkbox (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.atStart.note: Checkbox on a remembered USB device's line (Machines page, USB tab): the device is attached when the machine starts.

Usb.busy.asking.note: What the Machines page is doing (shown with … at its top) while the browser's chooser asks for a USB device's permission.

Usb.allow.title.message: Open this browser's device chooser, showing this device. Select it to give this web app permission to use it.
Usb.allow.title.note: Tooltip of a USB device's Allow… button (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.allow.note: Button on a remembered USB device this browser has no permission for (Machines page, USB tab): opens the browser's chooser.

Usb.busy.detaching.note: What the Machines page is doing (shown with … at its top) while a USB device is detached.

Usb.detach.title.message: Unplug the device from the guest.
Usb.detach.title.note: Tooltip of an attached USB device's Detach button (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.detach.note: Button on a USB device attached to the machine running in this tab (Machines page, USB tab): unplugs it from the guest.

Usb.busy.attaching.note: What the Machines page is doing (shown with … at its top) while a USB device is attached.

Usb.attachHere.title.message: Another machine is using the device. You will be asked before it is detached there.
Usb.attachHere.title.note: Tooltip of the Attach here… button on a USB device another machine holds (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.attach.title.message: Plug the device into the guest.
Usb.attach.title.note: Tooltip of a plugged-in USB device's Attach button (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.attachHere.note: Button on a USB device another machine holds, while this machine runs in this tab (Machines page, USB tab): asks, then takes it.

Usb.attach.note: Button on a plugged-in USB device while the machine runs in this tab (Machines page, USB tab): plugs it into the guest.

Usb.forget.button.title.message: Make this machine forget the device.
Usb.forget.button.title.note: Tooltip of a remembered USB device's Forget button (Machines page, USB tab).

Usb.forget.button.note: Button on each remembered USB device (Machines page, USB tab): the machine forgets it (asked first).

Usb.none.note: The Machines page's USB tab's list when the machine remembers no device.

Usb.builtin.pluggedNow.message: Connector {{connector}} belongs to the built-in keyboard. It passes the keys you press to the firmware and the boot loader, and is unplugged once the guest's own keyboard driver takes over. It is plugged in now.
Usb.builtin.pluggedNow.note: Note on the Machines page's USB tab, for the machine running on this page while its built-in keyboard is plugged in. {{connector}} is the keyboard's connector number (from 1).

Usb.builtin.asNow.message: Connector {{connector}} belongs to the built-in keyboard. It passes the keys you press to the firmware and the boot loader, and is unplugged once the guest's own keyboard driver takes over. It is unplugged now.
Usb.builtin.asNow.note: Note on the Machines page's USB tab, for the machine running on this page while its built-in keyboard is unplugged (the guest's driver took over). {{connector}} is the keyboard's connector number (from 1).

Usb.builtin.message: Connector {{connector}} belongs to the built-in keyboard. It passes the keys you press to the firmware and the boot loader, and is unplugged once the guest's own keyboard driver takes over.
Usb.builtin.note: Note on the Machines page's USB tab, for a machine that isn't running on this page. {{connector}} is the built-in keyboard's connector number (from 1).

Usb.add.note: Button under the remembered devices (Machines page, USB tab): opens the Add a USB device wizard.

Usb.twins.message: Identical devices without a serial number are told apart by the order this browser lists them in, usually the order they were plugged in. Plug them in in the same order every time, or the guest may see them swapped.
Usb.twins.note: Note on the Machines page's USB tab, shown when the machine remembers identical devices without a serial number.

Usb.note.otherTab.message: The machine is running in another tab; attach and detach devices there. Devices are plugged in and out while the machine runs, without orphaning its snapshots. Snapshot and Suspend ask, then unplug them first.
Usb.note.otherTab.note: Note at the bottom of the Machines page's USB tab while the machine runs in another tab.

Usb.note.stopped.message: Attach and detach devices while the machine runs in this tab, here or from the toolbar's USB menu. Devices are plugged in and out while the machine runs, without orphaning its snapshots. Snapshot and Suspend ask, then unplug them first.
Usb.note.stopped.note: Note at the bottom of the Machines page's USB tab while the machine isn't running.

Usb.note.message: Devices are plugged in and out while the machine runs, without orphaning its snapshots. Snapshot and Suspend ask, then unplug them first.
Usb.note.note: Note at the bottom of the Machines page's USB tab while the machine runs on this page.

UsbMenu.why.unplugged.note: Tooltip of a remembered device's line in the toolbar's USB menu when it isn't plugged in (its checkbox is off).

UsbMenu.why.heldBy.note: Tooltip of a remembered device's line in the USB menu when another machine, in another tab, has it. {{holder}} is that machine's name.

UsbMenu.why.held.message: Another machine is using the device.
UsbMenu.why.held.note: Tooltip of a remembered device's line in the USB menu when another machine, in another tab that didn't say its name, has it.

UsbMenu.why.ungranted.message: This browser has no permission to use the device yet. Allow it on the Machines page's USB tab.
UsbMenu.why.ungranted.note: Tooltip of a remembered device's line in the USB menu when this browser hasn't granted it (its checkbox is off).

UsbMenu.where.detaching.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu while it is being detached.

UsbMenu.where.attaching.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu while it is being attached.

UsbMenu.where.connector.note: Right side of an attached device's line in the toolbar's USB menu: the connector it is on. {{connector}} is its number (from 1).

UsbMenu.where.heldBy.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu when another machine has it. {{holder}} is that machine's name.

UsbMenu.where.held.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu when another machine (that didn't say its name) has it.

UsbMenu.where.ungranted.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu when this browser hasn't granted it.

UsbMenu.where.unplugged.note: Right side of a device's line in the toolbar's USB menu when it isn't plugged in.

UsbMenu.title.message: Attach USB devices to the machine, or add one.
UsbMenu.title.note: Tooltip of the toolbar's USB menu button.

UsbMenu.attached.note: Screen-reader name of the count badge on the toolbar's USB button. {{n}} is the number of devices attached (1 or more).

UsbMenu.notNow.note: Button of an offer at the top of the USB menu (a device plugged in, one unplugged, a permission to give): dismisses the offer.

UsbMenu.problems.message: Part of the device doesn't reach the guest. Hover here, or see All USB settings… for details.
UsbMenu.problems.note: Warning under an attached device in the toolbar's USB menu when part of it is kept from the guest; its tooltip lists what.

UsbMenu.none.note: The toolbar's USB menu's list when the machine remembers no device.

UsbMenu.pads.note: Heading in the toolbar's USB menu above the host's game pads that the browser lists (the Gamepad API), each with a checkbox that attaches it to the machine as a USB game pad.

UsbMenu.pads.none.message: Press a button on a game pad to list it here.
UsbMenu.pads.none.note: Hint under the USB menu's Game pads heading when the browser lists no game pad: browsers show a page a game pad only once one of its buttons has been pressed while the page is open.

UsbMenu.pad.why.message: Attach a USB game pad to the machine that follows this game pad's buttons, sticks and triggers. Use it for a game pad that can't be added as a USB device.
UsbMenu.pad.why.note: Tooltip of a game pad's line in the USB menu (under Game pads).

UsbMenu.zero.note: Name of the controller's test device in the USB menu (with ?usbzero=1), beside its checkbox.

UsbMenu.zero.note.note: What Gadget Zero is, at the right of its line in the USB menu (with ?usbzero=1).

UsbMenu.add.note: Button in the toolbar's USB menu: opens the Add a USB device wizard.

UsbMenu.all.note: Button in the toolbar's USB menu: opens the Machines page's USB tab for this machine.

UsbMenu.stopped.message: The machine isn't running. Devices marked At start that are plugged in will be attached when it starts.
UsbMenu.stopped.note: Hint at the bottom of the toolbar's USB menu while the machine isn't running.

AddUsb.usb.note: Title of the first choice in the Add a USB device wizard: a device passed through over WebUSB.

AddUsb.usb.text.message: Developer and maker hardware, passed through as it is: microcontroller boards and debug probes, Android phones (adb, fastboot), USB-serial adapters, logic analyzers, SDRs, and printers. Keyboards, mice, disks, webcams, headsets, and Bluetooth adapters can't be passed through, nor can an interface a driver on your computer holds. If a device has such parts, you will be told which, and what to do.
AddUsb.usb.text.note: Explanation under A USB device (WebUSB), the first choice in the Add a USB device wizard.

AddUsb.hid.note: Title of the second choice in the Add a USB device wizard: a device built from what WebHID tells.

AddUsb.hid.text.message: Game pads, joysticks and wheels, macro pads and Stream Decks, a keyboard's configuration interface (VIA), and UPSes, over USB or Bluetooth. The guest gets a USB HID device rebuilt from what this browser reports about it. A keyboard's keys and a mouse's pointer can't be passed through; your keyboard and mouse reach the machine through this emulator anyway.
AddUsb.hid.text.note: Explanation under A HID device (WebHID), the second choice in the Add a USB device wizard.

AddUsb.title.note: Title of the Add a USB device wizard (a dialog from the USB menu or the Machines page's USB tab). {{name}} is the machine's name.

AddUsb.step.kind.message: Choose the kind of device below.
AddUsb.step.kind.note: Step 1 of the Add a USB device wizard, numbered, above the two kinds to choose from.

AddUsb.step.pick.message: Select the device in the list this browser shows.
AddUsb.step.pick.note: Step 2 of the Add a USB device wizard, numbered, above the two kinds: the browser's chooser opens once a kind is chosen.

AddUsb.note.message: The machine remembers the device and attaches it at start, and this browser keeps the permission to use it. A machine running in this tab gets it right away.
AddUsb.note.note: Note under the two kinds in the Add a USB device wizard: what happens to the device picked.

AddUsb.noWebUsb.note: Tooltip of the disabled WebUSB choice in the Add a USB device wizard, in a browser without WebUSB.

AddUsb.noWebHid.note: Tooltip of the disabled WebHID choice in the Add a USB device wizard, in a browser without WebHID.

AddUsb.cancel.note: Button that closes the Add a USB device wizard without adding anything.

UsbProblems.details.note: Title of the folded details (a summary to click) under a USB problem that has no remedy of its own, only the browser's message.

usb-entries.machineGone.note: Error when a USB device's entry is changed for a machine that was deleted meanwhile (in another tab).

usb-actions.stopped.message: The machine isn't running in this tab. Start it to attach devices.
usb-actions.stopped.note: Error when a USB device is attached (the USB menu, the Machines page's USB tab) while the machine isn't running in this tab.

usb-attach.offer.gone.message: {{name}} was unplugged from connector {{connector}}. If it came back as another device, such as a bootloader after a firmware upload, pick that one to attach it on the same connector.
usb-attach.offer.gone.note: An offer in the toolbar's USB menu when an attached device was unplugged (Pick it… follows); {{name}} is the device's name, {{connector}} its connector's number.

usb-attach.offer.pick.note: Button of the USB menu's offer after a device was unplugged: it opens the browser's chooser for the device that came back.

usb-attach.detached.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when an attached USB device was detached by an error; {{name}} is the device's name; the error is the detail under it.

usb-attach.attachFailed.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a USB device couldn't be attached; {{name}} is the device's name; why is the detail under it.

usb-attach.attachFailed.again.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a USB device detached for a snapshot couldn't be attached again; {{name}} is the device's name; why is the detail under it.

usb-attach.held.left.message: {{name}} was left attached to {{who}}, in another tab.
usb-attach.held.left.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a device attached at start is attached to another tab's machine (left there); {{name}} is the device's name, {{who}} that machine's.

usb-attach.held.left.unknown.message: {{name}} was left attached to another machine, in another tab.
usb-attach.held.left.unknown.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a device attached at start is attached to another tab's machine whose name isn't known; {{name}} is the device's name.

usb-attach.held.confirm.message: Detach {{name}} from {{who}}, in another tab, and attach it here? That machine will see the device unplugged, and whatever it was doing with it will fail.
usb-attach.held.confirm.note: Text of the question asked when a USB device is attached here while another tab's machine has it; {{name}} is the device's name, {{who}} that machine's.

usb-attach.held.confirm.unknown.message: Detach {{name}} from another machine, in another tab, and attach it here? That machine will see the device unplugged, and whatever it was doing with it will fail.
usb-attach.held.confirm.unknown.note: Text of the question asked when a USB device is attached here while another tab's machine, whose name isn't known, has it; {{name}} is the device's name.

usb-attach.held.title.note: Title of the question asked when a USB device is attached here while another tab's machine has it.

usb-attach.held.ok.note: The confirm button of the question asked when a USB device is attached here while another tab's machine has it.

usb-attach.held.kept.message: Couldn't take {{name}} from {{who}}, in another tab
usb-attach.held.kept.note: Error headline when another tab's machine didn't give up a USB device asked for here; {{who}} is that machine's name, {{name}} the device's.

usb-attach.held.kept.unknown.message: Couldn't take {{name}} from the machine in another tab
usb-attach.held.kept.unknown.note: Error headline when another tab's machine, whose name isn't known, didn't give up a USB device asked for here; {{name}} is the device's name.

usb-attach.taken.message: {{name}} was detached, because another machine took it.
usb-attach.taken.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) when another tab's machine took a USB device from this one; {{name}} is the device's name.

usb-attach.keyboardFailed.message: Couldn't plug in the built-in keyboard
usb-attach.keyboardFailed.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when the page's built-in USB keyboard (for the firmware and boot loaders) couldn't be attached; why is the detail under it.

usb-attach.offer.ungranted.message: This browser has no permission to use {{name}} yet, because the machine was set up in another browser.
usb-attach.offer.ungranted.note: An offer in the toolbar's USB menu for a remembered device the browser hasn't allowed (Allow… follows); {{name}} is the device's name.

usb-attach.offer.allow.note: Button of the USB menu's offer for a device without permission: it opens the browser's chooser for it.

usb-actions.offer.plugged.note: An offer in the toolbar's USB menu when a device was plugged into the computer; {{name}} is the device's name.

usb-actions.offer.attach.note: Button of the USB menu's offer for a remembered device that was plugged in: it attaches it.

usb-actions.offer.remember.note: Button of the USB menu's offer for a device the machine doesn't remember that was plugged in: it attaches it and remembers it.

usb-actions.offer.back.message: {{name}} just appeared where {{was}} was, on connector {{connector}}.
usb-actions.offer.back.note: An offer in the toolbar's USB menu when a device appeared right after an attached one was unplugged (a bootloader after a firmware upload); {{name}} is the new device's name, {{was}} the old one's, {{connector}} the connector's number.

usb-actions.offer.there.note: Button of the USB menu's offer for a device that appeared where another was: it attaches it on that connector.

usb-attach.empty.list.note: Several USB devices named in the question asked before a snapshot or Suspend: {{first}} is all of them but the last (joined with commas), {{last}} the last.

usb-attach.empty.snapshot_one.message: Taking a snapshot needs the USB ports empty. This will detach {{list}}, and the guest will see it unplugged; anything in progress with it, such as a copy or a firmware flash, will fail. It will be attached again once the snapshot is saved.
usb-attach.empty.snapshot_one.note: Text of the question asked by Snapshot or Save snapshot while a USB device is attached; {{list}} is its name.

usb-attach.empty.snapshot_other.message: Taking a snapshot needs the USB ports empty. This will detach {{list}}, and the guest will see them unplugged; anything in progress with them, such as a copy or a firmware flash, will fail. They will be attached again once the snapshot is saved.
usb-attach.empty.snapshot_other.note: Text of the question asked by Snapshot or Save snapshot while USB devices are attached; {{list}} is their names, {{count}} how many.

usb-attach.empty.suspend_one.message: Suspending needs the USB ports empty. This will detach {{list}}, and the guest will see it unplugged; anything in progress with it, such as a copy or a firmware flash, will fail. If it is marked At start, it will be attached again when the machine resumes.
usb-attach.empty.suspend_one.note: Text of the question asked by Suspend while a USB device is attached; {{list}} is its name.

usb-attach.empty.suspend_other.message: Suspending needs the USB ports empty. This will detach {{list}}, and the guest will see them unplugged; anything in progress with them, such as a copy or a firmware flash, will fail. Those marked At start will be attached again when the machine resumes.
usb-attach.empty.suspend_other.note: Text of the question asked by Suspend while USB devices are attached; {{list}} is their names, {{count}} how many.

usb-attach.empty.title.note: Title of the question asked by Snapshot, Save snapshot or Suspend while USB devices are attached.

usb-attach.empty.ok.note: The confirm button of the question asked by Snapshot, Save snapshot or Suspend while USB devices are attached.

usb-actions.edit.detachFirst.message: Detach the device before changing its connector.
usb-actions.edit.detachFirst.note: Error when an attached USB device's connector is changed (the Machines page's USB tab).

usb-actions.zero.stopped.message: The machine isn't running with a USB controller.
usb-actions.zero.stopped.note: Error of the test device's switch (`?usbzero=1`, the USB menu) when the machine isn't running with a USB controller.

usb-actions.zero.full.note: Error of the test device's switch (`?usbzero=1`, the USB menu) when no connector is free.

usb-actions.pad.full.message: The game pad wasn't attached, because every USB connector is in use.
usb-actions.pad.full.note: Error of a game pad's checkbox in the USB menu when no USB connector is free.

usb-actions.pad.gone.message: The game pad wasn't attached, because it is no longer connected to your computer.
usb-actions.pad.gone.note: Error of a game pad's checkbox in the USB menu when the browser no longer lists that game pad.
